ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean by 'Hammaz' and 'Masha' bin Namim'?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this phrase from Surah Al-Qalam is often linked to the specific traits of the disbelievers who opposed the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), with some scholars identifying it as referring to Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah. The term 'namim' (gossip) specifically denotes carrying words between people to cause enmity, highlighting a destructive social sin that undermines community cohesion. This description serves as a moral warning against those who spread discord and slander, a theme frequently echoed in the Ahl al-Bayt's teachings on character.
